findings.description: SqliteFTS5Dialect.matchClause/scoreClause (fts-dialect.ts:195-211, pre-existing on main, unchanged by this branch) HARDCODE `fts_node` and ignore the `table` parameter, while the new A2 surface (ftsSearch/ftsCount/ensureFtsIndex) documents and accepts a general `table`. On sqlite the composed SQL is `FROM fts_${table} JOIN ${table} n ... WHERE fts_node MATCH ? ... -fts_node.rank AS score` — correct only for table='node'. For table='episode'/'claim': if fts_node does not exist → loud 'no such table'; if fts_node DOES exist (normal memory store) → silently wrong join-filter, no error. Turso honors `table` correctly (index lives on the base table), so the API behaves differently per backend for the same call. No current or planned caller passes a non-node table (memory-core FTS_DDL/graph-store FTS is fts_node only; all 19 tests use 'node'), so there is no live breakage — but the published interface over-promises. Fix options: plumb `table` into matchClause/scoreClause (dialect interface change), or document sqlite-node-only in the FtsSearch/FtsCount/FtsEnsure JSDoc + CHANGELOG. Can ride into the next release; does not warrant a 0.4.1 patch on its own.
findings.fix_sketch: Either (a) add `table: string` to FTSDialect.matchClause/scoreClause and emit `fts_${table} MATCH ?` / `fts_${table}.rank` in SqliteFTS5Dialect, or (b) narrow the documented contract: 'SQLite FTS5 path supports the graph-store fts_<table> shape; non-node tables only on Turso' and assert/throw on mismatch.

findings.description: In finishEnsureFtsIndex the residue-drop loop catches `/already exists/i` on statements from dialect.dropLegacyDDL — but those are DROP statements with IF EXISTS guards (fts-dialect.ts:178-185, 286-291), which never raise 'already exists'. The skip is dead code; a real DROP failure rethrows (correct). Not a bug, but the regex copy-pasted from the CREATE path is misleading. Cosmetic.
findings.fix_sketch: Remove the try/catch or narrow it to a comment explaining IF EXISTS makes the skip unnecessary.

findings.description: resolveExistingFtsIndexName returns the FIRST sqlite_master row whose sql matches /using\s+fts/i. If a store somehow carries BOTH the canonical idx_fts_node AND a repaired idx_fts_node__r1 (creation order puts canonical first), the adoption branch in ensureFtsIndex (fts-ops.ts:244) sees the canonical name, does NOT adopt, and the orphan survives → permanently doubled write/storage cost — the exact silent symptom BL-461 exists to prevent. The intended BL-461 repair path (canonical dropped, only _r1 remains) is handled correctly and is tested; this both-exist edge is not. Not reachable through current flows.
findings.fix_sketch: If a non-canonical FTS index is found while the canonical also exists, report it (e.g. return the list of FTS indexes and let ensureFtsIndex drop/adopt the orphan) — or document that coexistence requires out-of-band cleanup.

findings.description: MockAdapter.ensureFtsIndex reports `backfilled: true` whenever `opts.backfill !== false`, but nothing is actually backfilled (the mock keeps no index — by design). A consumer asserting on `backfilled` against the mock gets a semantically different signal than against real backends. Acceptable for a test double; note it in the JSDoc.
findings.fix_sketch: Document that mock `backfilled` is a bookkeeping echo, or set it to false.
